What is Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery?

Cosmetic eyelid surgery involves the removal or repositioning of excess skin, fat, and muscle from the upper and lower eyelids. This procedure addresses common concerns such as drooping eyelids, under-eye bags, and wrinkles, resulting in a more alert and youthful appearance. Cosmetic eyelid surgery can be performed on the upper eyelids, lower eyelids, or both, depending on your specific needs and goals.

The Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons utilize advanced techniques to ensure the best possible outcomes for cosmetic eyelid surgery. The procedure involves:

Upper Eyelid Surgery

An incision is made along the natural crease of the upper eyelid to remove excess skin, muscle, and fat, resulting in a smoother and more lifted appearance.

Lower Eyelid Surgery

An incision is made just below the lower lash line or inside the lower eyelid (transconjunctival approach) to remove or reposition excess fat, smooth out wrinkles, and tighten the skin.

The choice of technique will depend on your specific concerns and aesthetic goals, which will be thoroughly discussed during your consultation.

What to Expect After Surgical Eye Rejuvenation

View More Before & After Results

Recovery from cosmetic eyelid surgery is typically smooth, with most patients experiencing mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Cold compresses and prescribed medications can help manage these symptoms. Most patients return to their normal activities within 10-14 days. The final results, which can be seen as swelling subsides, include a more youthful and rejuvenated appearance with brighter, more alert eyes.

Frequently Asked Questions | Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery

What Concerns Can Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery Address?

Cosmetic eyelid surgery can address drooping upper eyelids, under-eye bags, puffiness, and wrinkles, providing a more youthful and refreshed appearance.

Is Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery Covered by Insurance?

Cosmetic eyelid surgery is typically considered an elective procedure and is not covered by insurance. However, if the surgery is performed to improve vision or address a medical condition, insurance may cover some or all of the costs.

Who is a Good Candidate for Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery?

Ideal candidates are individuals with realistic expectations who are in good overall health and have concerns about sagging eyelids, under-eye bags, or wrinkles around the eyes.

What Can I Expect During Recovery?

Recovery involves mild swelling and bruising, which typically subsides within one to two weeks. Most patients can return to their normal activities within 10-14 days.

Are There Risks Involved with Cosmetic Eyelid Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

How Soon Will I See Results After Surgery?

Initial results can be seen as swelling and bruising subside, typically within two weeks. Full results, showcasing a smoother and more youthful eye area, will be visible in a few months.
